topics.topic: Exact request_digest header set: only kernel-defined headers or also transport/client-added headers (including multipart boundary-dependent Content-Type details)
questions: Does "every header the kernel sends" include transport/client-added headers (for example Host, Content-Length, multipart boundary headers), or only headers explicitly set by kernel rules?

Which headers are part of that set for digest comparison: only headers explicitly built by kernel rules, or also transport/client-added headers (for example Host, Content-Length, User-Agent, boundary-dependent headers)?
When a multipart request is approved, is the `Content-Type` boundary parameter (and other transport-added header details) part of the approval-covered request or ignored for digest matching?

judgement.divergence: One implementation computes `request_digest` from only the headers explicitly constructed by kernel rules, while another includes all headers actually sent on the wire (including transport/client-added headers such as `Host`, `Content-Length`, `User-Agent`, or multipart `Content-Type` details); owners and agents notice because the same logical send may or may not require a new approval.
judgement.why: The text does not close whether transport-layer or client-library-added headers are part of "every header the kernel sends" for approval matching.

topics.topic: Deterministic multipart/form-data metadata for non-file/value parts (e.g., per-part Content-Type/charset/filename) and whether it must be stable for approval matching
questions: What media type must be set (or considered) for non-file multipart parts, so request construction and request_digest are deterministic?

What exact multipart part metadata must be emitted (for example Content-Disposition filename parameter, per-part Content-Type for value parts, charset), and are these details required to be stable for approval matching?

judgement.divergence: One implementation emits fixed multipart metadata for non-file parts (stable media type/charset/filename behavior) and keeps request digests stable, while another leaves non-file part metadata to library defaults that vary by runtime or version; external services and owners/agents notice via different service acceptance and different approval re-ask behavior.
judgement.why: The rules require multipart parts to include name, media type, and content hash but do not specify the required media type/metadata conventions for non-file parts tightly enough to force one behavior.

topics.topic: How to handle 2xx response bodies when a binding has zero output ports (parse/validate/read with limits vs ignore)
questions: For a non-file binding with no output ports, must a 2xx response body still parse as a JSON object, or is any body accepted/ignored?
If a binding has zero output ports, must the kernel still read and enforce response-body ceilings, or may it ignore the body entirely?

judgement.divergence: One implementation always reads and validates a 2xx body (size limits and JSON-object parsing) even when a binding has zero output ports, while another ignores the body entirely for zero-output bindings and treats 2xx as success; owners and agents notice different node statuses (`contract_violation` vs `succeeded`) and run outcomes.
judgement.why: The rules leave open whether "a binding without output ports ignores the body" overrides the general non-file 2xx body parsing and size-validation requirements.

topics.topic: Required kernel behavior when a store call fails during run advancement or owner actions (refuse/continue vs terminate vs special run state)
questions: When such a store call fails during run advancement or owner actions, must the kernel return a refusal and keep running, or terminate process (like A03 cleanup failure), or mark affected runs specially?

topics.topic: Whether guarded-but-currently-disabled incoming edges should count toward upstream_failed when their source fails
questions: When an input has guarded incoming edges, should a failed source count for upstream_failed if that edge is currently disabled by guard?

topics.topic: Whether repeating the same path placeholder name multiple times is allowed (reuse same input) or is a manifest mismatch/refusal
questions: If the same `{name}` appears multiple times in a path, is that allowed (same input substituted each time) or a manifest mismatch/refusal?

topics.topic: Whether standing grants for non-stopping classes (read/normal draft-write) are allowed and storable as inert or must be refused
questions: Are standing grants for `read` or normal `draft-write` nodes valid and storable (but inert), or should such grant requests be refused as nonsensical?
